posts.title: How Long Does Botox Last? A Realistic Timeline From Day 1 to Month 4
posts.dek: When results show up, when they fade, and the habits that make a difference, explained by the team that injects every day in Pittsburgh.
posts.imgAlt: Botox consultation at Avere Beauty med spa
posts.seoTitle: How Long Does Botox Last? Timeline & Tips | Avere Beauty Pittsburgh
posts.seoDesc: Most Botox results last 3 to 4 months. See the day-by-day timeline, what makes it wear off faster, and how to plan touch-ups from a Pittsburgh med spa.
takeaways: Most people see results begin in 3 to 5 days and peak around 2 weeks.
Results typically last 3 to 4 months, sometimes longer in less active areas.
Dose, muscle strength, metabolism and consistency all change how long it lasts.
A 2-week check-in is the right time to adjust, not day 3.

body.x: Botox is the most requested treatment at Avere Beauty, and "how long will it last?" is the question we hear most. The short answer is 3 to 4 months for most people. The longer answer depends on where it is placed, how much is used, and how your body processes it. Here is what actually happens after your appointment, week by week.
What Botox does

Botox Cosmetic is a purified protein that temporarily relaxes the muscles that crease your skin when you frown, squint or raise your brows. It does not fill or plump. When the muscle moves less, the line it creates softens. It was first FDA-approved for frown lines in 2002 and is now one of the most studied cosmetic treatments in the world.

Botox is one of several neurotoxins. Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau and Daxxify work the same basic way, with small differences in how quickly they start and how long they tend to last. Your injector will recommend one based on your goals and history.
The timeline, day by day

head: When
What you'll notice
rows: Small bumps at injection sites that settle within about 30 minutes. You can return to normal activity, skipping workouts for the rest of the day.
Movement starts to soften. Many people notice it first when they try to frown.
Full effect. This is when your injector judges the result and adds a touch more if needed.
Peak smoothness holds. Lines that were etched in may keep improving because the skin is no longer folding.
Movement gradually returns. Most people book their next visit here.

body.title: Why we check in at two weeks
body.x: Botox takes time to settle. Judging the result on day 3 often leads to adding product that wasn't needed. At two weeks, what you see is the real result.
Why it lasts longer for some people
Two people can get the same treatment and have different results. These are the factors that matter most:

items: Dose. Too little product for a strong muscle wears off sooner. Your injector balances a natural look with longevity.
Muscle strength. Strong frown muscles, common in men and very expressive faces, often need more units.
Area. Forehead lines can fade sooner than frown lines because the forehead uses a lighter dose to keep brows from dropping.
Metabolism. Very active people and endurance athletes sometimes report shorter results.
Consistency. Many clients find that with regular treatments, the muscle is used less over time and results feel longer.

body.x: The goal isn't a frozen face. It's looking rested, with your expressions still yours.
How to make it last

items: Stay upright and skip heavy workouts for the rest of the day.
Don't rub or massage the treated area for 24 hours.
Wear sunscreen daily. UV damage deepens lines that Botox is trying to soften.
Pair it with skincare. Retinoids and medical-grade products work on texture while Botox works on movement.
Book before it fully wears off. Starting from partial effect usually feels smoother than starting over.

body.x: Preventative Botox

Some clients in their twenties and early thirties choose small doses before lines are etched in. The idea is to soften movement so creases form more slowly. It isn't necessary for everyone. A consultation will tell you whether the lines you see at rest are worth treating now or worth waiting on.
Planning around events
For weddings, photos or big events, book at least two weeks ahead so you're at full effect and have time for an adjustment. Four weeks ahead is even safer if it's your first time.

faq: How long does Botox take to work?
Most people notice softening in 3 to 5 days, with full results at about 2 weeks.
How long does Botox last?
Typically 3 to 4 months. Some areas and some people hold results longer or shorter.
Does Botox last longer the more you get it?
Many clients find results feel longer with consistent treatments, because the muscle is used less over time. It varies by person.
What happens if I stop getting Botox?
Movement returns gradually and your lines return to how they would have looked without treatment. Stopping doesn't make wrinkles worse.

posts.title: Lip Filler Swelling and Aftercare: A Day-by-Day Guide
posts.dek: What's normal on day one, day three and week two, plus the aftercare habits our injectors actually recommend.
posts.imgAlt: Lip filler aftercare essentials at Avere Beauty
posts.seoTitle: Lip Filler Swelling & Aftercare Day by Day | Avere Beauty
posts.seoDesc: Lip filler swelling usually peaks in 24 to 72 hours and settles within 2 weeks. A day-by-day guide to what's normal and how to care for your lips.
takeaways: Swelling usually peaks in the first 24 to 72 hours.
Most swelling settles within a week; your final shape shows at about 2 weeks.
Cold compresses, sleeping elevated and skipping workouts for 24 to 48 hours help.
Call your injector about severe pain, blanching or skin color changes.

body.x: Lip filler results look best at two weeks, but the first few days can be surprising if you don't know what to expect. Swelling, tenderness and a little unevenness are a normal part of healing. Here is what each stage usually looks like and what you can do to stay comfortable.
Why lips swell after filler

Most lip fillers are made of hyaluronic acid, a sugar your skin already makes. It attracts water, which is part of how it creates volume. Lips also have a rich blood supply and thin skin, so the small needle passes and the product itself trigger a short inflammatory response. That combination is why lips swell more than other treated areas.
The timeline

head: When
What's typical
rows: Lips look full and may feel firm. Some tenderness and pinpoint bruising.
Swelling peaks. Lips can look larger or uneven, often more so in the morning.
Swelling eases noticeably. Bruises fade from purple to yellow.
Filler softens and integrates. The final shape and size become clear.
Ideal time for a follow-up if anything needs adjusting.

body.title: Uneven in the first week is usually swelling
body.x: One side often swells more than the other. Wait the full two weeks before judging symmetry. Your follow-up visit is the right time for any fine-tuning.
Aftercare that helps

items: Use a clean cold compress for 10 minutes at a time during the first day.
Sleep with your head slightly elevated for the first two nights.
Skip intense workouts, saunas and hot yoga for 24 to 48 hours.
Avoid alcohol for the first day; it can increase swelling and bruising.
Don't press, massage or pucker hard unless your injector tells you to.
Keep lips moisturized with a clean, gentle balm applied without rubbing.

body.x: Our founder created Avere Cosmetics' post-injection lip balm for exactly this window. It has a touch-free applicator, so you never press on tender injection sites, and arnica and aloe in a non-sticky gloss. You can pick one up at your appointment or online.
What to avoid

items: Dental work for two weeks before and after, when possible.
Lipstick and lip liner on day one.
Straws and smoking for the first 24 hours.
Flying on day one if you can plan around it.

body.x: When to call us

Complications are rare, but you should call your injector right away for severe or worsening pain, skin that turns white, gray or dusky, a lace-like pattern on the skin, or blisters. These need same-day attention. You can reach Avere Beauty at 412-952-7592.
How long lip filler lasts
Most lip filler lasts about 6 to 12 months, depending on the product, how much was placed and your metabolism. Many clients maintain with a smaller touch-up once or twice a year.

faq: How long does lip filler swelling last?
Most swelling peaks in 1 to 3 days and settles within about a week. Final results show at around 2 weeks.
Is it normal for lips to look uneven after filler?
Yes, in the first week. Swelling is rarely symmetrical. Judge the result at 2 weeks.
Can I work out after lip filler?
Wait 24 to 48 hours before intense exercise to limit swelling and bruising.
What should I put on my lips after filler?
A clean, gentle balm applied without pressing. Avoid lipstick on day one.

posts.title: Dry vs. Dehydrated Skin: How to Tell the Difference and Fix Each One
posts.dek: They look alike and feel alike, but they need different care. A clinical guide to what your skin is actually missing.
posts.imgAlt: Medical-grade skincare products at Avere Beauty
posts.seoTitle: Dry vs. Dehydrated Skin: How to Tell & What Helps | Avere Beauty
posts.seoDesc: Dry skin lacks oil; dehydrated skin lacks water. Learn the signs, a simple at-home test, and the ingredients and treatments that help each one.
takeaways: Dry skin is a skin type: it makes less oil.
Dehydration is a condition: skin is short on water, and any skin type can have it.
Dry skin needs oils and barrier repair; dehydrated skin needs humectants and less stripping.
HydraFacial and medical-grade products can help both.

body.x: If your skin feels tight, looks dull or shows fine lines that weren't there last month, you might call it dry. It could also be dehydrated. The difference matters, because the fix for one can make the other worse.
Dry skin: low on oil

Dry skin is a skin type. Your oil glands produce less sebum, so the skin's protective layer is thinner. It tends to feel rough, can flake, and often stays this way year-round. Genetics, age and conditions like eczema all play a role.
Dehydrated skin: low on water

Dehydration is a temporary condition. Your skin isn't holding enough water, even if it still makes oil. That's why oily and acne-prone skin can be dehydrated too. Harsh cleansers, over-exfoliating, winter heating, travel, alcohol and some acne medications are common causes.

head: Sign
Dry skin
Dehydrated skin
rows: Dull, crepey, fine lines appear quickly
Can still be oily or breaking out

body.x: A simple at-home test

Gently pinch the skin on your cheek. If it wrinkles finely and stays creased for a second, it's likely dehydrated. You can also wash with a gentle cleanser and wait 30 minutes without products. Dry skin feels rough and may flake. Dehydrated skin feels tight but may still look shiny in the T-zone.
How to treat dry skin

items: Use a cream cleanser and skip foaming or gel cleansers.
Choose moisturizers with ceramides, fatty acids and cholesterol to rebuild the barrier.
Add a facial oil at night if you're very dry.
Exfoliate gently, no more than once or twice a week.

body.x: How to treat dehydrated skin

items: Look for humectants like hyaluronic acid and glycerin, applied to damp skin.
Seal them in with a light moisturizer so the water doesn't evaporate.
Pause harsh scrubs and strong acids until your skin feels comfortable again.
Run a humidifier in winter and drink water consistently.

body.title: Don't strip oily skin to fix breakouts
body.x: Over-cleansing oily skin can dehydrate it, which can trigger even more oil. A balanced routine usually clears skin faster than an aggressive one.
Treatments that help

A HydraFacial cleanses, gently exfoliates and infuses hydrating serums in about 30 minutes, which makes it a good reset for both. SkinPen microneedling supports collagen and helps skin hold moisture over time. Our estheticians can also build a medical-grade routine for your skin type, which tends to deliver more active ingredients than drugstore options.

faq: Can oily skin be dehydrated?
Yes. Dehydration is about water, not oil, so oily and acne-prone skin can still be dehydrated.
Is hyaluronic acid good for dry skin?
It helps hold water, but dry skin also needs oils and barrier-repair ingredients like ceramides.
Does drinking water fix dehydrated skin?
It helps, but topical humectants and a gentle routine matter more for the skin's surface.
What facial is best for dehydrated skin?
A HydraFacial is a popular choice because it hydrates while it cleanses and exfoliates.

posts.title: How to Get Rid of Acne: What Works, What Doesn't, and When to Get Help
posts.dek: From the right cleanser to in-office treatments, a clear plan for breakouts at any age.
posts.imgAlt: Skin treatment at Avere Beauty med spa in Pittsburgh
posts.seoTitle: How to Get Rid of Acne: A Clinical Guide | Avere Beauty Pittsburgh
posts.seoDesc: What causes acne, which ingredients work, how long to give them, and the in-office treatments that help clear breakouts and scarring in Pittsburgh.
takeaways: Acne comes from four things: oil, clogged pores, bacteria and inflammation.
Give any new routine 8 to 12 weeks before judging it.
Benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid and retinoids are the proven starting points.
Painful, cystic or scarring acne deserves a medical visit.

body.x: Acne is the most common skin condition in the country, and it doesn't end with your teens. Many adults deal with breakouts for the first time in their twenties, thirties or later. The good news: acne is very treatable once you know what is driving it.
What causes acne

Four things work together. Your oil glands produce sebum. Dead skin cells mix with that oil and clog the pore. Bacteria that normally live on skin multiply in the clogged pore. Your body responds with inflammation, which creates red, tender bumps. Hormones, stress, some medications and certain products can turn any of these up.
Types of breakouts

head: Type
What it looks like
Usually responds to
rows: Red bumps, some with white centers

body.x: The ingredients that work

items: Benzoyl peroxide reduces acne bacteria. Start with 2.5% to limit irritation.
Salicylic acid dissolves oil inside pores, helpful for blackheads.
Retinoids, including over-the-counter adapalene, keep pores from clogging and are a long-term foundation.
Azelaic acid calms redness and helps with marks left behind.

body.title: Patience is part of the treatment
body.x: Most acne treatments take 8 to 12 weeks to show their full effect, and skin can look worse for the first few weeks on a retinoid. Changing products every week keeps you stuck at the starting line.
Habits that help

items: Cleanse twice a day with something gentle. Scrubbing harder doesn't clear pores faster.
Choose non-comedogenic moisturizer and sunscreen.
Change pillowcases often and clean your phone screen.
Don't pick. Picking pushes inflammation deeper and raises the risk of scars and dark marks.

body.x: In-office treatments

When a home routine isn't enough, professional treatments can speed things up. Chemical peels exfoliate and unclog pores. HydraFacial deep-cleans and extracts. For the marks and scars acne leaves behind, SkinPen microneedling, Subnovii and laser resurfacing can improve texture over a series of sessions.
Avere Beauty also offers advanced acne solutions through our medical team, including options for persistent and hormonal breakouts. A consultation will sort out which approach fits your skin.
When to see a medical provider

items: Deep, painful nodules or cysts.
Acne that leaves scars or dark marks.
Breakouts that haven't improved after three months of consistent care.
Sudden adult acne along with irregular cycles or other hormonal symptoms.

faq: How long does it take to get rid of acne?
Expect 8 to 12 weeks with a consistent routine before judging results.
Does diet cause acne?
For some people, high-glycemic foods and dairy may play a role. It varies, so changes are worth discussing with a provider.
Can facials help acne?
Yes. HydraFacials and chemical peels can clear congestion and support a home routine.
How do I get rid of acne scars?
Microneedling, Subnovii and laser resurfacing can improve texture over several sessions.

posts.title: Can You Get Kybella for the Stomach? What It's Approved For and What Works Better
posts.dek: Kybella is built for the double chin. Here's why, and which options make more sense for stubborn belly fat.
posts.imgAlt: Kybella treatment guide from Avere Beauty
posts.seoTitle: Can You Get Kybella for the Stomach? | Avere Beauty Pittsburgh
posts.seoDesc: Kybella is FDA-approved for fat under the chin, not the stomach. Learn why, what the risks of off-label use are, and better options for belly fat.
takeaways: Kybella is FDA-approved only for fat under the chin.
Using it on the stomach would require many vials and isn't studied for that area.
For stubborn belly fat, body contouring and medical weight management are more practical.
A consultation helps match the treatment to the area and your goals.

body.x: Kybella works so well under the chin that many clients ask the natural next question: can it do the same thing for my stomach? It's a fair question. The answer comes down to how Kybella works and what it was designed for.
How Kybella works

Kybella is an injectable form of deoxycholic acid, a molecule your body uses to break down dietary fat. Injected into a small pocket of fat, it disrupts fat cell membranes. Your body then clears those cells over the following weeks. Because destroyed fat cells don't come back, results in the treated area are long-lasting when weight stays stable.
What it's approved for
The FDA approved Kybella in 2015 for one area: moderate to severe fat beneath the chin, often called a double chin. That approval is based on studies of that specific area, dose and technique.
Why the stomach is different

items: Size. The abdomen holds far more fat than the chin. Treating it would take many vials per session and many sessions.
Swelling. Kybella causes significant swelling and tenderness. Over a large area, that adds up.
Evidence. There isn't strong research on safety and results for the abdomen.
Cost. The number of vials needed makes it an expensive way to treat a large area.

body.title: Small areas only
body.x: Even when providers use Kybella off-label, it's typically for small, defined pockets of fat, not the whole stomach. Your provider will tell you honestly whether an area is a good fit.
Better options for belly fat
If your goal is a flatter stomach, a few approaches tend to make more sense:

items: Medical weight management. Our NP-led program can include prescription options when appropriate, along with guidance and check-ins.
CryoSkin. A non-invasive cooling treatment used for body contouring and toning, with no downtime.
Lifestyle foundations. Sleep, protein intake and strength training affect where your body stores fat.

body.x: Who Kybella is great for

Kybella is a strong choice for people at a stable weight who have a stubborn pocket of fat under the chin that doesn't respond to diet and exercise. Most people need 2 to 4 sessions spaced about a month apart. Expect swelling for several days after each one.

faq: Is Kybella approved for the stomach?
No. Kybella is FDA-approved only for fat under the chin.
How many Kybella sessions do I need for a double chin?
Most people need 2 to 4 sessions, spaced about a month apart.
Are Kybella results permanent?
Treated fat cells are destroyed, so results are long-lasting if your weight stays stable.
What's better than Kybella for belly fat?
Medical weight management and body contouring treatments like CryoSkin are more practical for the stomach.
